hypothesis: The built-in templates, with no game knowledge, die before 5:00 on the Nightmare Daily, and the log shows which damage sources and which minutes do it.
test: Play the templates as they are; change nothing. This is the baseline every later run compares with.
outcome: Lived 18:20 on DG0S-Z730R0, level 75, 73630 kills. At 4:56 and 5:02, level 21 at 60/129. Damage: hot oil 274, ketchup-kraken 193, compost-titan 144, deep-freezer 82, amusing 46, grater-golem 16, blight-spore 14, spore vent 4. End row 17/129, Ketchup Kraken 289 away, no hit logged after 18:10. The end detail says survived 18:20.
learnings: On this seed the built-in templates live far past 5:00. They evade from 0:05 to 1:13, aside from a 3-second explore at 1:02 (enemies_near 0, a crate 31 away ignored, hot oil ticking) and then collect gems, with chest bursts that finish recipes: Permafrost Fries at 2:09, Overgrowth at 4:38, Big Fry at 10:14, Baked Alaska at 11:26, Hungry Sprouts at 14:24. The picker stacks a held card and also takes a new weapon when it scores higher (Locked Gatling 4:15, Reset Button 11:35, Fry Knives 15:17). Frozen Fries also won a level-up at 38% against 33% at 1:05. Reroll and Skip never won a listed pick. Damage is hot oil and bosses, not the crowd. Boss minutes: amusing 2:00-2:09, chest kept, hp 105 to 57, contact. Deep Freezer from 14:00, gems kept, drops of about 20 at 14:08 (move), 14:12 (plan row, no move) and 14:16 (move), about 62 of 82; hp rose from 84 at 14:12 to 113 at 14:16 with no food goal. Grater Golem 16:00-16:12, gems kept, one hit of 16, boss to 1%, hp back to 129 by 16:05. The Masher (4:01), Sir Strawman (7:03), The Great Wireworm (10:00) and The Mandoline (12:04) are absent from the damage outcome. Compost Titan from 17:03, evade chosen, hits of 62, 32 and 21 while the boss was about 180 away (about 115 of 144), then chunk heals back to 129 by 17:33. Ketchup Kraken from 18:04, 64 hp with no move row (116 to 52) and 34 more by the food row at 18:10 (to 17 hp); about 98 of 193. The 18:20 row is still 17 hp. Display names match those ids on the same rows. A chest channel failed at 4:32 because stand-still was ruled out by extraDamage (forecast -4 to -7, gold 510) and the fail text blamed gold; the same chest became Overgrowth at 4:38. Health also jumps about 30 with no food goal, including during the freezer and the titan. From 9:16 to 9:24 the planner swapped two Spud Freezers that had tied at 57%. One sample.

hypothesis: Taking every chest and shrine in reach makes Tibo stronger faster than it costs in health.
test: planner.state tells the planner to favour chests and charge spots over gems and evading whenever they are within reach, and to pick the highest-damage card.

hypothesis: Favouring food, evading, and health and armor cards carries a weak build further than the baseline.
test: planner.state tells the planner to evade whenever enemies are close, eat food under 70% health, and pick health and armor first.

hypothesis: Planning every pick around one evolution, and saving chests until it is ready, beats picking for kill speed now.
test: planner.state names one weapon and its catalyst from the encyclopedia and tells the planner to take only those until the recipe is ready.

hypothesis: Exploring for chests and spots beats collecting xp gems.
test: planner.state favours explore goals over gems; knobs.exploreDistance 600.

hypothesis: Not every spot that charges helps: some (a Beetle Nest wakes an elite) cost more than they give.
test: Send Tibo to every kind of spot it meets once, and read the log around each for health, level and enemies after.

hypothesis: The planner follows a directive written into planner.state: its picks and goals change when the directive does.
test: Write one plain directive into planner.state and count how many picks and goals in the log agree with it.

hypothesis: Asking the action model less often (a higher extraDamage) costs little health, because the game's forecast already rules out the worst moves.
test: knobs.extraDamage 0.08 against the baseline 0.02; compare health lost per minute.

hypothesis: When a boss first appears, evading away from it loses less health than going for a chest or gems near it.
test: planner.state tells the planner that a boss nearby means the next goal is evade, away from the boss. Everything else stays as the baseline. Compare health across the minute after the boss appears with E1. E1's contact case is amusing at 2:00 (chest kept, hp 105 to 57 by 2:09). E1 already chose evade at 17:03 for Compost Titan and still lost about 115 hp by 17:14 while the boss was about 180 away, so that minute is a separate question and a gain there should not be read as the amusing result. Grater Golem (16:00, 16 damage, boss to 1% by 16:12 while gems continued) is the case where evading would have to beat a cheap minute. Also record hp lost across The Masher (4:01), Sir Strawman (7:03), The Great Wireworm (10:00) and The Mandoline (12:04): on E1 none of those names appear in the damage outcome, so an evade-all rule has to beat minutes that cost about nothing. Same-day Nightmare Daily only.

hypothesis: A weapon that hits all around Tibo without needing a direction (Steam Vent) is a better first weapon on nightmare than whatever card looks strongest.
test: planner.state names Steam Vent and tells the planner to take it first, then Root Network, and to open a chest once that recipe is ready. One directive, nothing else changed.

hypothesis: Taking Rotten Spud on nightmare ends the run sooner, because the curse brings harder enemies before its evolutions pay off.
test: planner.state tells the planner to take Rotten Spud the first time it appears, and to play the baseline otherwise.

hypothesis: Telling the action model to leave hot oil, and telling the planner not to evade while no enemy is within 60 and no boss is close, cuts hot-oil damage well below the baseline 274 and still lives past 5:00.
test: action.hurt and action.useful treat a move that stays on burn ground as worse than a move that steps off it, unless stepping off is forecast to hurt more than a scratch. planner.goal: with enemies_near at 0 and no boss within 200, a chest or gems outranks evade. Knobs unchanged. Compare hot-oil damage with E1's 274, and whether the run is still alive at 5:00. Same-day Nightmare Daily only.

hypothesis: A chest Tibo is already opening fails because stand-still is ruled out when staying forecasts more than extraDamage, and offering that step, then telling the model to stay unless the next second would kill Tibo or a boss is in contact, removes those failed opens.
test: The 4:32 failure is the filter, not the model's choice: stand still forecast about -4 to -7 hp and was ruled out, while walking off forecast about 0. extraDamage 0.02 of 129 is about 2.6 hp, so a template that praises standing still never sees that move. Raise extraDamage to 0.06 so a -7 forecast can be offered, and change action.hurt and action.useful: on a chest already charging, standing still is the useful move and counts as a scratch, unless the forecast says Tibo dies or a boss is in contact. Two changes, because the prompt cannot choose a move the knob removes. Count goals that fail with "standing there did nothing" against E1's failure at 4:32, and record the first evolution time (E1: Permafrost Fries 2:09, Overgrowth 4:38).

hypothesis: boss:ketchup-kraken and boss:compost-titan are bosses that appear after the Deep Freezer on this daily, and their damage is what takes a finished baseline build from full to dead at 18:20.
test: No template change. On the next run, read the first row where hurt_by contains each of those ids and record the bosses named on that same row, the clock time, and the hp drop. Leave the result inconclusive if the id and the display name are never on one row. Compare the totals with E1 (193 and 144) only if the run is another baseline.
outcome: Answered from E1's own log. Compost Titan is boss:compost-titan, first at 17:03 (90 down, 47%). Hits at 17:09 (62, boss 184 away at 1%), 17:10 (32) and 17:14 (21), about 115 of 144, during an evade goal. Ketchup Kraken is boss:ketchup-kraken, first at 18:04 (144 down-right, 84%, hp 116 to 52, no move row) and 18:10 (to 17 hp), about 98 of 193. The 18:20 row is still 17/129 with the kraken 289 away and no new hit.
learnings: The names and the order are settled on this seed: Deep Freezer at 14:00, Compost Titan at 17:03, Ketchup Kraken at 18:04, and the id sits on the same row as the display name. Grater Golem matches boss:grater-golem at 16:04. amusing matches boss:amusing. Colorado Queen shares the 3:05 row with boss:beetle-queen 2.2 (lead). The killing-blow clause is not in the log. The titan damage was followed by chunk heals to 129 at 17:33. The kraken left Tibo at 17 hp at 18:10, and the end row ten seconds later shows that same 17 with hp_lost 0. The end detail says survived 18:20. About 29 of the titan's 144 and about 95 of the kraken's 193 are not on a sampled row. One sample. Do not spend another run only to learn the names.

hypothesis: The baseline's rises of about 25 to 30 hp with no food goal are a repeating heal, and they are why a run that sat at 49/129 from 3:05 still reached 5:00 and why Compost Titan's hits at 17:09 did not end it.
test: No template change. On the next run, list every rise of 10 hp or more that has no food goal beside it, with the clock time. Name the source only if heals are logged by source. Compare those times with E1: 57 at 2:11 to 83 at 2:17, 49 at 3:53 to 75 at 3:58, 55 at 4:15 to 84 at 4:20, 73 at 6:47 to 103 at 6:52, 92 at 7:23 to 122 at 7:28, 103 at 9:36 to 129 at 9:41, 84 at 14:12 to 113 at 14:16 during the Deep Freezer and before the food goal, 35 at 17:10 to 65 at 17:12, and 45 at 17:17 to 75 at 17:20 to 105 at 17:21 (two chunks about 2 seconds apart, before the Lean Lunch card was taken). Same-day Nightmare Daily only.

hypothesis: A completed food goal heals about 30 hp, and the 18:10 eat is an exception because a boss hit landed in the same seconds.
test: No template change. On the next run, for every food goal that ends eaten, record hp on the start row and the done row, and any boss in hurt_by. E1: 5:50 at 49 to 5:53 at 79, 14:17 at 88 to 14:18 at 118, 16:45 at 125 to 16:46 at 129, and 18:07 at 52 to 18:10 at 17 with boss:ketchup-kraken on the row. Same-day Nightmare Daily only.

hypothesis: Grater Golem is a cheap boss: staying on gems costs about 16 hp and the boss is nearly dead within 20 seconds, so a rule that evades every boss is wrong for this one.
test: Baseline templates, no new directive. If Grater Golem appears, record hp lost from the first row that names it until 20 seconds later, and the boss's health on that later row. E1: first named 16:00 at 178 up-left and 100%, hit of 15.6 at 16:04, hp 129 at 16:05, boss 1% at 16:12. Inconclusive until a second daily shows the same boss. Same-day Nightmare Daily only.

hypothesis: Once the planner is charging a spot, switching to a second copy of the same spot spends the channel time and does not change the result.
test: planner.state tells the planner to keep charging the spot it is already on until that spot finishes, and not to switch to another of the same kind. Everything else stays the baseline. Count spot goals dropped before they finish. E1 swapped P89 and P95 from 9:16 to 9:24, both scored 57% at 9:16, and one freezer finished at 9:24 with hp still 106.

hypothesis: Under the built-in templates, nightmare open world matches the daily baseline: the planner evades, then collects gems, and nearly all damage comes from hazards and bosses rather than the crowd.
test: Change nothing. Same planner, action and knobs as E1. On this open-world run, record the goals through the first two minutes, enemies_near, and the outcome damage by source. Confirm if those goals are evade then gems and hazards plus bosses are most of the damage. Refute if the opening goals are something else, or if crowd and other non-boss contact damage is the largest source. Do not compare clocks or totals with the daily. One sample. A heal of about 25 to 30 hp with no food goal is a lead, not part of the result.
outcome: Lived 3:16 on nightmare-1 world seed 2R6JH5, died at level 9 with 822 kills, hp 120 to 1. Baseline templates and knobs were unchanged, and the top score won every pick and every goal. Opening goals were evade, explore and one Spud Freezer. Gems never started. Damage list is eight trash enemies summing to 96, with no hazard and no boss.
learnings: The bot played the test. 8 of 8 level-ups match the top card, and every goal start matches the top goal score, including explore up at 0:32 (40% over evade 39%) and a 41% tie at 1:26 that went to explore up-right. In the first two minutes evade started 13 times, explore 3 times and the Spud Freezer once. Across the run: 22 evade starts, 4 explores (the 0:32 walk found nothing; explores at 1:06, 1:26 and 2:19 were dropped at the next card or plan), 1 freezer used at 0:58, and 0 gems, 0 food and 0 chests. Gems first appear on the list at 0:32 and peak at 42% at 1:06, one point behind explore. enemies_near is 4 at 0:08 and often above 0 after that, so the daily picture of a crowd that never comes within 60 does not happen here. Food is offered from 1:18 (185 left, 23%) through 1:47 (30%) while hp is 103 to 96, then leaves the list. A chest is first offered at 2:16, 66 left, at 22%, and chests score 32% and 19% at 2:37 with hp 43, always under evade. Weapons end at Rösti Disc 3/8 and Frying Pan 3/8, Lean Lunch 2/5, Chives 1/5, no items, no evolution. Listed damage: snow-mold 19, cave-grub 18, compost-maggot 15, sand-crab 11, fry-fly 10, oil-drip 8, frost-flea 8, potato-beetle 7, sum 96, against a fall from 120 to 1. The gap of about 23 is unaccounted. The steep losses are 93 to 72 from 1:55 to 1:57 and 61 to 29 from 2:32 to 2:42, during evade, on steps the forecast often calls free (9 hp at 1:56, 5 at 1:57, 4 at 2:32, 2:36, 2:50, 3:00 and 3:01). amusing is on screen from 2:00 to about 2:33 and Colorado Queen from 3:00 to the end, and neither is on the damage list. Hp never jumps; the daily's unexplained +25 to +30 does not appear. Evade rows say kept clear for 8 seconds at 0:45, 1:55, 2:03, 3:04 and 3:12 while hurt_by is set or hp is already 3 or 1. The run_end detail says survived 3:16 while the notes say died, on 1 hp, the same end-row mismatch as the daily. One sample. Clocks and totals are this run's own.

hypothesis: On nightmare open world, steps the one-second forecast calls free still take 2 hp or more, often enough that the action model's safest choice is where the crowd damage lands.
test: No template or knob change is required for the measurement, so record it on the next nightmare world run whatever else that run tests. Count chosen move rows whose forecast says no damage and whose hp_lost is 2 or more. This run: 9 hp at 1:56, 5 at 1:57, 4 at 2:32, 4 at 2:36, 4 at 2:50, 4 at 3:00, 4 at 3:01, and repeated losses of 2 from 0:49. Confirm if a second world run has several such rows in its first three minutes. Refute if chosen no-damage steps lose about 0. Seeds may differ.

hypothesis: On nightmare open world the baseline dies around 3 minutes because evade keeps beating chests and food. Telling the planner to open a listed chest, and to eat when health is under 70%, gets a chest open and leaves Tibo alive past 3:16.
test: Change planner.state only. Action templates and knobs stay the baseline. Directive, near the top: when a chest is listed, open it; when health is under 70% and food is listed, eat it; evade only when no chest and no food is listed. Nightmare open world. Count chests opened and hp at 3:16. This run: 0 chests, food offered 1:18 to 1:47 and never taken, dead at 3:16 on 1 hp, weapons still 3/8. Confirm if at least one chest opens and hp is above 1 at 3:16. Refute if the run is dead by 3:16 with no chest opened. One sample. Seeds may differ, so a single win is a lead.

hypothesis: The daily's unexplained rises of about 25 to 30 hp do not happen on nightmare open world in the first three minutes.
test: No template change. On the next nightmare world run, list every rise of 10 hp or more with no food goal beside it. This run had none from 0:00 to 3:16 while hp fell from 120 to 1 and max hp stayed 120. The daily's first such rise was at 2:17. Confirm if a second world run also has none by 3:00. Inconclusive if the run ends before 2:00. A rise of about 25 to 30 refutes it.

hypothesis: On nightmare open world, amusing around 2:00 and Colorado Queen around 3:00 put no damage on the outcome list, and the trash mobs do.
test: No template change. On the next nightmare world run, record the first row that names each boss and whether that name is on the outcome damage list, plus hp across the first 30 seconds of the fight. This run: amusing 2:00 at 100% to gone by 2:33, hp 72 to 53, no amusing line; Colorado Queen 3:00 at 100% to 73% at 3:15, no queen line. Confirm if a second run's bosses are also absent from the damage list. Inconclusive if no boss spawns. Refute if a boss name leads the damage list.
